speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, have you noticed any changes in your weight, and are you experiencing any pain in your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of alcohol use and the painless nature of your current symptoms, I need to check for pancreatic involvement. REQUEST TEST: CA 19-9, CT Abdomen/Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CA 19-9 and CT scan make pancreatic cancer unlikely, so we should look for other causes of biliary obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound, Liver Function Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Bilirubin Total 5.6 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 192 U/L, AST 32 U/L, ALT 34 U/L. Abdominal Ultrasound reveals an anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region with dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of a subhepatic cystic mass with bile duct dilation are highly suggestive of a choledochal cyst. To confirm the anatomy and rule out other biliary pathologies, I will request further imaging. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily. Does this smoking history continue to the present day, or have you quit recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Episode of acute upper abdominal pain treated three years ago. History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking. Social history: Stopped alcohol consumption three years ago; 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a cystic mass causing biliary obstruction, which is concerning for a choledochal cyst or cholangiocarcinoma given your age and smoking history. To better visualize the biliary tree and the nature of this mass, I need more detailed imaging. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP is unexpected given the ultrasound findings, suggesting the mass may be vascular or pancreatic in origin rather than biliary. Let's proceed with an ERCP to directly visualize the ducts and potentially biopsy any suspicious lesions. REQUEST TEST: ERCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the conflicting imaging results and persistent obstructive symptoms, I suspect a choledochal cyst that may have been misinterpreted or obscured in previous scans. REQUEST TEST: HIDA Scan, Endoscopic Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP and ERCP effectively rule out intrinsic biliary obstruction or malignancy, so the ultrasound likely misidentified a vascular structure as a cystic mass. REQUEST TEST: Doppler Ultrasound of the Abdomen

speaker: Doctor
text: With all structural, vascular, and functional tests returning normal despite clear signs of obstructive jaundice, this clinical picture of painless jaundice, pruritus, and weight loss in an elderly male is classic for cholangiocarcinoma, likely at the hilum where imaging can be deceptive. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cholangiocarcinoma
